caption: The AI wanted line breaks and bold text in comments, so it rendered them as HTML. It works, and it's a security hole. Look at the card. When you write {comment.text}, React escapes it, so any HTML tags show up as plain text. dangerouslySetInnerHTML skips that. If someone posts a comment like , the browser runs that code for every person who views the page. That's XSS (cross-site scripting). If you really need formatted comments, convert them on purpose (a markdown library) and sanitize the HTML with a library like DOMPurify before rendering. The prop is named "dangerously" for a reason. Treat it as a review flag. Source: react.dev, Common components (dangerouslySetInnerHTML).
